script-opening-jsx.comment: A tag written where a script's body begins. TypeScript's own JSX rules start a tag only after one of the tokens an expression can follow — `(`, `=>`, `return`, a line start — and a body starts after a backtick, which is none of them; without this a script whose first thing is an element reads as arithmetic, `<` a less-than and the tag a variable. Every later line starts one, so the base grammar has them from there. The tag rules below are the base grammar's own, and they are ungated on purpose — `x < y` at the end of a line matches one — so what this adds is the gate: after the backtick only, where an expression cannot begin with `<` and a tag is the only thing it can be, and closed again at the `>` that ends the element. The one borrowed guard is TypeScript's, for a generic parameter list: `<T,>` and `<T extends U>` open no tag.
